title: Rational stalk Frobenius powers along a closed-point orbit
statement:
Fix the global finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$ and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite. Let $X_0$ be separated of finite type over $k_0$, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $(K_E,\varphi_E)$ be an $E$-Weil complex [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], with an integral representative whose reductions are in $D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)$. Use the $E$-stage stalk operators and their specified normalized stalk transports from [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model]. Let $x\in|X_0|$ be a closed point, $e=[\kappa(x):k_0]$, and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. A lift is a $k$-morphism $z:s\to X$ above $x$. Put $\sigma(c)=c^q$, $\gamma=\sigma^{-1}$ and $g=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$. For any starting lift $z_0$, enumerate the lifts by $z_i=g^iz_0\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma^i)$, $0\le i<e$. Denote by $y_{i,m}\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ the rational point represented by $z_i$ when $e\mid m$. Put $F_x=F_{y_{0,e},e}$ on the rational stalk complex $K_{E,z_0}$. Then there are $E$-linear isomorphisms of stalk complexes $T_i:K_{E,z_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}K_{E,z_0}$, with $T_0=1$, such that for every $r\ge1$,
$$F_{y_{i,er},er}=T_i^{-1}F_x^rT_i\qquad(0\le i<e).$$
In particular the conjugacy class of $F_x$ is independent of the starting lift. The equality uses the normalized fixed-point operators, including the source reparametrization displayed above. Only invertibility of $\varphi_E$ in $D^b_c(X,E)$ is assumed; no invertible Weil structure on an integral lattice is required.

source.place: Step 1, Local powers: rational stalk transport, cyclic products and conjugacy to powers of the one-circuit operator

proof.text:
Apply only clause (1) of [lem-trf-local-frobenius-conjugacy], with the zero strict Weil complex over $A_1$ (zero complex, unique isomorphism $Lg^*0\cong0$, as in [def-trf-strict-weil-complex]). This clause concerns the lifts alone: there are exactly $e$ of them, $z_i=G^iz_0$, with $G(v)=gv\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$ and $z_{i+e}=z_i$; for $e\mid m$ each is the lift of the specified $y_{i,m}$. No reduction of $\varphi_E$ is used here. The affine formulas in [def-trf-scheme-frobenius] give, for $v^*(a\otimes b)=v_0^*(a)b$,
$$(Gv)^*(a\otimes b)=\sigma(v_0^*(a)\gamma(b))=v_0^*(a)^q b=(\Phi v)^*(a\otimes b).$$
Thus $\Phi v=Gv$ for every $k$-point $v$, and $\Phi^m z_i=z_i$ for $e\mid m$. Also $g^mz_i=z_i\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma^m)$, as an equality of scheme morphisms; the unreparametrized map $g^mz_i$ is not identified with $z_i$.

source.place: Step 1, Local powers, with the orbit comparison and cyclic-product argument written explicitly

proof.text:
Use [lem-trf-completed-stalk-reparametrization-coherence] over $E$. For any $k$-point $v$ and $i\ge0$ define the natural isomorphism
$$Q_i^v(M)=c_{g^i,v,M}^{-1}r_{g^iv,\sigma^i,M}^{-1}:M_{G^iv}\longrightarrow(L(g^i)^*M)_v.$$
The identity equations give $Q_0^v=1$. Its composition and reparametrization equations give, under the specified pullback comparison,
$$Q_{i+j}^v(M)=Q_i^v(L(g^j)^*M)Q_j^{G^iv}(M).$$
Indeed the two inverse $r$ maps remove the source automorphisms $\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma^j)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma^i)$; these commute and compose to $\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma^{i+j})$. Move the first reparametrization across the pullback comparison by the displayed $r$–$c$ square of the cited lemma, and combine the two inverse $c$ maps by its composition equation. The resulting map is precisely $c_{g^{i+j},v,M}^{-1}r_{g^{i+j}v,\sigma^{i+j},M}^{-1}$.

source.place: Step 1, Local powers, with the orbit comparison and cyclic-product argument written explicitly

proof.text:
Put $P_i=L(g^i)^*$ and $\varphi^{[0]}=1$. The $E$-stage definition in [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model] is the ordered composite $\varphi^{[n]}=\varphi_E P_1(\varphi_E)\cdots P_{n-1}(\varphi_E)$. The composition comparisons are associative and unital by [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization], also after rationalization. Splitting this ordered list after its first $i$ factors therefore gives
$$\varphi^{[i+j]}=\varphi^{[i]}P_i(\varphi^{[j]})\quad(i,j\ge0).$$
More explicitly, the $j=0$ case uses the identity comparison; adjoining $P_{i+j}(\varphi_E)$ to both sides of the identity for $j$ gives the identity for $j+1$, since functoriality identifies the last factors with $P_i(\varphi^{[j+1]})$. This induction uses no finite-coefficient Weil structure. Each factor is invertible because $\varphi_E$ is invertible in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex].

source.place: Step 1, Local powers, with the orbit comparison and cyclic-product argument written explicitly

proof.text:
Define $T_i^v=\varphi^{[i]}_vQ_i^v(K_E):K_{E,G^iv}\xrightarrow{\sim}K_{E,v}$ for every $i\ge0$. Steps 2–3 give $T_0^v=1$. Naturality from [lem-trf-completed-stalk-reparametrization-coherence], applied to $\varphi^{[j]}:P_jK_E\to K_E$, says
$$Q_i^v(K_E)\varphi^{[j]}_{G^iv}=(P_i\varphi^{[j]})_vQ_i^v(P_jK_E).$$
Consequently
$$T_i^vT_j^{G^iv}=\varphi^{[i]}_v(P_i\varphi^{[j]})_vQ_i^v(P_jK_E)Q_j^{G^iv}(K_E)=\varphi^{[i+j]}_vQ_{i+j}^v(K_E)=T_{i+j}^v.$$
All arrows in this equation go from $K_{E,G^{i+j}v}$ to $K_{E,v}$. The zero-index cases follow from the identity comparisons. These transports are indexed by integers and are not asserted to be periodic.

source.place: Step 1, Local powers, with the orbit comparison and cyclic-product argument written explicitly

proof.text:
Fix $v=z_i$, $e\mid m$, and $y=y_{i,m}$. The normalization theorem [lem-trf-local-frobenius-transport-normalization] identifies the actual normalized $\tau_{y,m}$ with the $m$ successive point transports along $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ on $Lv^*K_E$, followed by the composition comparison for $g^mv=vh^m$. Apply the source-automorphism equation $c_{\delta,\mathrm{id},N}j_{\delta,N}=r_{\mathrm{id},\alpha,N}$ of [lem-trf-completed-stalk-reparametrization-coherence] successively to these $m$ maps, and use its compatibility with $v$ and composition. It gives
$$c_{g^m,v,K_E}\tau_{y,m}=r_{v,\gamma^m,K_E}:K_{E,v}\longrightarrow K_{E,g^mv}.$$
Since $g^mv=v\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma^m)$, the $r$ composition equation identifies this right-hand side with $r_{g^mv,\sigma^m,K_E}^{-1}$. Therefore $\tau_{y,m}=Q_m^v(K_E)$. The $E$-stage operator formula in [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model] now gives
$$F_{y,m}=\varphi^{[m]}_v\tau_{y,m}=T_m^v.$$
The normalization theorem applies to the actual rationalized comparisons and assumes no integral Weil isomorphism. Its fixed-point equality is valid here by step 1, and its coefficient datum agrees with the given one.

source.place: Step 1, Local powers, with the orbit comparison and cyclic-product argument written explicitly

proof.text: For each $v=z_i$, step 1 gives $G^ev=v$. Step 4 with indices $e$ and $(r-1)e$ therefore gives $T_{re}^v=T_e^vT_{(r-1)e}^v$. Starting at $r=1$ and inducting yields $T_{re}^v=(T_e^v)^r$ for every $r\ge1$. By step 5, $T_e^{z_0}=F_{y_{0,e},e}=F_x$ and $F_{y_{0,er},er}=F_x^r$. This is a product identity of endomorphisms of the rational stalk complex, before passing to cohomology or traces.

source.place: Step 1, Local powers, with the orbit comparison and cyclic-product argument written explicitly

proof.text:
Set $T_i=T_i^{z_0}$ for $0\le i<e$. For $m=er$, the two decompositions from step 4, together with $G^mz_0=z_0$ and $G^iz_0=z_i$, give
$$T_iT_m^{z_i}=T_{i+m}^{z_0}=T_{m+i}^{z_0}=T_m^{z_0}T_i.$$
Steps 5–6 replace the two $T_m$ maps by $F_{y_{i,er},er}$ and $F_x^r$. Multiplying on the left by the inverse of $T_i$ gives exactly $F_{y_{i,er},er}=T_i^{-1}F_x^rT_i$, and $T_0=1$. For $r=1$ every other starting lift is one of the $z_i$ by step 1, so its one-circuit operator is conjugate to $F_x$. All inverses used are rational stalk isomorphisms from step 4; nothing requires an invertible map on an integral lattice.

split_report.summary: Expanded the rational-stage local-powers argument without applying finite-coefficient Weil results to a rational structure. One statement-only auxiliary node isolates completed stalk/reparametrization coherence, independently of any Weil map. Explicitly constructed Q_i and T_i, proved their composition identities, identified the specified normalized operators, and calculated powers and conjugacy. No statement change and no integral Weil isomorphism hypothesis.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes thm-trf-l-function-euler-product.proof.md Step 1, Local powers: (a) is the explicit regrouping in step 3; (b) is the auxiliary coherence node with the existing all-stage normalization used in steps 2 and 5; (c) supplies invertibility in steps 3–4. The conjugacy-of-operators assertion is proved directly in steps 6–7; trace invariance (d) is unnecessary for this stronger operator assertion.

tool_uses.why: Only coefficient-independent clause (1), instantiated with the zero finite Weil complex, supplies the closed-point orbit; none of its finite Weil operator clauses is used.
Supplies the actual rational iterates and normalized stalk operator formulas; it assumes an arbitrary rational morphism and does not impose integral invertibility.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-ND-8b093f45e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node, every cited statement, blueprint Step 1 (Local powers) and Stacks 05V1, 0F4F and 0993 in full; the item statement is unchanged. Batch-5 check: the item is the Euler-product local-powers regrouping, not a step of the trace formula. I computed the dependency closures of the four newly cited nodes. None reaches the trace-formula theorems (finite-ring, E, Qlb or local-term), either assumption leaf or any Poincaré-duality theorem. lem-trf-local-frobenius-conjugacy is used only for clause (1), the lifts of a closed point; its closure adds general categorical-trace algebra and finiteness of H_c, which is a hypothesis of the assumption, not a conclusion. The completed-stalk coherence node, the pullback-comparison realization and the transport normalization are comparison and operator-normalization coherence that neither assumption gives. Math: Φv=Gv rechecked on rings; Q_{i+j} rederived from the r–c square, the r composition law (Spec is contravariant) and the c composition law; the cocycle follows by naturality for rational morphisms; c∘τ=r_{v,γ^m}=r^{-1}_{g^mv,σ^m} gives τ=Q_m^v and F_{y,m}=T_m^v; powers and conjugacy have correct orientation. The new node is statement-only and self-contained, its equations are germ-level true, it is not a clause of the item, and grep for 'reparametri' found no duplicate (the existing coherence node is finite-ring only). One sentence in it ('compatible with any finite succession...') is vague, but everything step 5 needs follows from its displayed equations, so I left it. Edge cases checked: e=1, e=2, a non-integral φ_E, K=0 and empty X_0. Both declared tool_uses lie inside the unit route, so neither is needed and I accept none. No SGA. No changes.
